item.title: Former Diddy Prosecutor Jacqueline Kelly To Lead Cornell Assault Probe
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Jacqueline Kelly, a former Diddy prosecutor, will lead New York's reopened criminal probe into Cornell assault allegations.
item.content:encoded:
Jacqueline Kelly, the former federal prosecutor who helped oversee the sex-crimes case against Sean “Diddy” Combs, has been tapped to lead New York’s reopened criminal investigation into sexual assault allegations at Cornell University.

New York Attorney General Letitia James named Kelly as outside counsel for the probe. Kelly, a Cornell alumna and partner at Boies Schiller Flexner, will work with lawyers and investigators from her firm and the attorney general’s office to collect evidence, interview witnesses, review prior records and analyze the law.

Kelly will report to James, whom Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed special prosecutor on October 1 after saying she had lost confidence in Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten. Van Houten declined to bring charges in 2024 before reopening the matter after a former student filed a civil lawsuit in September.

“With her criminal legal expertise, commitment to public service, and judicial experience, I am confident that she will lead a fair and comprehensive investigation,” James said in a statement reported by The Associated Press.

The former student, identified in court papers as Jane Doe, alleges that several men raped her at a fraternity party in October 2024 after she was pressured to use ketamine and marijuana and drank alcohol that left her too intoxicated to consent. She later reported the incident to campus police and Cornell’s Title IX office. The allegations have not resulted in criminal charges, and the reopened investigation is expected to take months.

Two men named as defendants in the civil lawsuit have asked to remove James from the criminal probe, arguing that a social media post she made before her appointment showed bias. A judge has not ruled on that request.

James said when she accepted the special-prosecutor assignment that the inquiry would follow the evidence. “Every New Yorker deserves to know that when they report a crime, it will be investigated fully and fairly,” she said in an October statement.

Cornell says its own Title IX process was separate from any criminal review. “Cornell’s process is distinct from the criminal justice system and applies university policies and standards, not criminal law,” the school said in an updated public FAQ. Cornell said its hearings produced sanctions including expulsions and suspensions, while the Chi Phi chapter involved in the allegations was closed in 2024 and remains barred from campus.

The university has also hired former Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates to conduct an independent review of Cornell’s response and later gave survivors the option to choose New York State Police or Cornell Police for criminal investigations. Kelly’s appointment adds a new outside team to the criminal inquiry, but it does not resolve the allegations or determine whether charges will be filed.

item.title: Lil Nas X Celebrates Democratic Sweep With Abortion Joke
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Lil Nas X turned Democrats' 2026 midterm sweep into a five-word abortion joke as Congress and statehouses shifted left.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Nas X celebrated the Democratic Party’s 2026 midterm sweep with five words that instantly put his sense of humor back in the political conversation.

“WE ALL GETTING ABORTIONS TONIGHT!” the Grammy-winning artist wrote on X after the election results rolled in Wednesday (November 4).

The joke landed after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress. The Associated Press reported the party flipped at least seven Senate seats and more than two dozen House districts, including races in places Donald Trump carried comfortably in 2024.

The results also reached deep into state government. Democrats won governor’s races in Georgia, Ohio, Iowa and Texas, while the party gained or kept full control in several states.

The sweep produced a string of firsts, including the country’s first Black female governor, first Native American female senator and first Muslim senator.

The same election map kept reproductive rights in view: Idaho voters rejected an abortion-rights measure, and incoming Democratic majorities have listed healthcare and abortion protections among their priorities.

That is familiar ground for an artist who has used short, high-impact posts to make larger arguments about sexuality, religion and who gets to police public behavior.

The post also came during a personal and professional reset.

Lil Nas X returned on October 1 with “World’s Greatest,” his first new song of 2026.

The video was filmed in Atlanta and dedicated to his late mother, Tamikia Hill. In announcing it, he repeated her advice to “walk by faith, not by sight.”

The song followed months of treatment and therapy after his 2025 arrest and hospitalization.

In April, a Los Angeles judge said felony battery charges would be dismissed if he completed a two-year mental health diversion program. By June, the rapper said he was doing better and working toward new music.

Now his first big political reaction since that return is a one-line joke tied to a result with real consequences: Democrats will enter 2027 able to block legislation, reject nominees and investigate the Trump administration from Capitol Hill.

item.title: Fabolous Wants A Bar-Heavy Drake Project And Confirms New Music
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Fabolous wants a more lyrical Drake project, explains his competitive feature mindset and confirms new music is on the way.
item.content:encoded:
Fabolous wants a Drake project built on bars. During an interview on “Cousins with Vince Carter & Tracy McGrady”, the veteran rapper said he wants to hear Drake lean further into his lyrical side.

Fabolous also explained why he sees guest verses as a contest and confirmed that new music of his own is coming.

His request was about the writing. He wants Drake to make a full project with tight lyrics and more bars.

That fits how Fabolous described his own work on guest spots. He treats each feature as a contest. He measures his verse against what is already on the song. On “Cousins,” he linked that drive to a wider point: artists have to grow rather than lean on an old formula.

That outlook goes back to the mixtape circuit that shaped his early-2000s run.

Fabolous said mixtapes “also used to be more raw, more street gritty, or more freestyle over other people’s beats.”

That helps explain why he still values songs where the verse is the main event.

In 2026, Fabolous has tied his music history to the work he is doing now. “The Hoodoos (Freestyle)” is his latest release, dated September 17.

One week later, he joined “Joe and Jada” to mark 25 years since Ghetto Fabolous arrived on September 11, 2001. He also discussed his move into “Let’s Rap About It” with Jim Jones, Dave East and Maino.

He said artists should control their stories and keep Hip-Hop history alive.

There is also a business side to his promise of new music.

AllHipHop reported in November 2025 that Fabolous had spent nearly two years untangling an old deal. He gave no release date or project title.

However, he confirmed that new music is coming. What it will sound like and when it will arrive remain open.

item.title: Russell Brand Convicted Of Rape And Three Sexual Assaults
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Russell Brand was convicted of rape and three sexual assaults in London and will be sentenced at Southwark Crown Court Monday.
item.content:encoded:
Russell Brand was convicted of rape and three sexual assaults in London and taken into custody ahead of sentencing.

A jury at Southwark Crown Court returned the four guilty verdicts Thursday after more than eight hours of deliberations across two days, according to The Associated Press.

The British comedian and actor was acquitted of two other rape counts and one count of attempted indecent assault. The case involved six women and allegations that stretched from 1999 to 2009.

Judge Joel Bennathan refused bail and remanded Brand in custody. The judge said Brand faces a “significant” prison term when he is sentenced Monday, November 9.

Brand, 51, denied every charge. He testified that he had lived a promiscuous life but had never forced anyone into sexual activity. He told the court, “My entire life has been consumed by these events, these allegations, these accusations.”

Prosecutors argued that Brand used his growing fame and status to target women. The guilty verdicts covered one rape and three sexual assaults committed between 2004 and 2009 at locations that included his home, a radio station and a recording set.

The Metropolitan Police said investigators spoke with more than 100 witnesses, took more than 400 statements and reviewed over 1,400 documents while rebuilding events that happened years earlier.

“Brand used his influence, status and fame to exploit and sexually offend against women,” Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy said after the verdict.

The investigation began after allegations were reported by Channel 4’s Dispatches, The Times and The Sunday Times in September 2023. The women in those reports were not the complainants in this criminal trial.

Two additional charges were authorized in December 2025 after separate reports involving alleged incidents in 2009. The Crown Prosecution Service said at the time that those reports concerned two other women.

Police said two further rape allegations remain under investigation. Detective Inspector Laura Nelson, who led the case, told Reuters, “My opinion is that he is a sexual predator and he has abused his power throughout his career.”

Brand rose through British stand-up, television and radio before appearing in Hollywood films including Forgetting Sarah Marshall and Get Him to the Greek. He later built a large online following around politics, wellness and religion.

His sentence will turn the jury’s verdict into the court’s final punishment. Until then, Brand remains in custody and the separate police investigations remain open.

item.title: Doja Cat Paints Dallas Blue After Democratic Midterm Sweep
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Doja Cat changed a "Paint The Town Red" lyric to blue during her Dallas concert after Democrats swept the midterm elections.
item.content:encoded:
Doja Cat gave “Paint The Town Red” a political rewrite during her Dallas concert, changing the hit’s closing line to celebrate the Democratic Party’s midterm victories.

As the song reached its final bars Wednesday night, Doja delivered the altered lyric: “I don’t care, I paint the town BLUE!” Video of the moment at American Airlines Center quickly spread online.

The change was brief, but it was clear.

Doja did not turn the show into a campaign speech or make a broader endorsement from the stage.

She used one of her biggest records to acknowledge an election result that had already become a major cultural conversation.

Democrats regained control of both the House and Senate in the midterm elections, prompting reactions from entertainers across music, film and television.

Doja’s response came in Texas, where the Dallas stop landed one night after the vote.

The November 4 concert was part of her Tour Ma Vie World Tour, with Latto billed as the special guest. The run supports Doja’s fifth studio album, Vie, and continues through San Antonio on November 6 and Houston on November 7 before moving east.

Live Nation announced the North American dates in September 2025, when Vie arrived. The North American leg began October 1 in Detroit and is scheduled to close December 1 at Madison Square Garden in New York, making the Dallas performance one stop in Doja’s largest international headlining run.

The Dallas moment also arrived during a revealing stretch for Doja.

In August, she spoke openly about a past cocaine problem while discussing her mental health. In October, she brought Rico Nasty out during her Los Angeles birthday show for a surprise “Tia Tamera” reunion.

Those appearances followed her May disclosure that she was considering a three-year break from music once the tour ends.

She said the time away could include family plans and a return to visual art.

For now, the tour is still moving. Dallas got a one-line political detour before Doja returned to the show, leaving the audience with a version of “Paint The Town Red” that belonged to that night.

item.title: Shyheim Calls Out Fat Joe & Funk Flex Over Alleged Blacklisting
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Shyheim is questioning Fat Joe and Funkmaster Flex over an old conversation he seems to interpret as blocking his opportunities as a teen.
item.content:encoded:
Shyheim wants an explanation for a joke that apparently never felt funny from his side.

The former Rugged Child is revisiting a conversation involving Fat Joe and Funkmaster Flex, and his concern goes beyond somebody laughing at his name. In the statement posted on Facebook, he accuses the two of discussing how to shut a teenager out of opportunities.

“In the 1990s, two grown men were on the phone discussing how to blacklist a 15-year-old kid and prevent him from accessing opportunities.

Let that sink in.

A child navigating an industry dominated by adults, politics, egos, and power plays.

Welcome to the music industry.

Some stories don’t need embellishment. The truth speaks loudly enough.”

That is a serious accusation, so the context deserves some attention.

For all the context, we have to take a step way back. A 2017 report about Joe’s interview with Flex describes a discussion about getting Big Pun onto Flex’s compilation. According to that account, Flex had been refusing crew affiliates, with Shyheim and King Just mentioned as examples. That supports the existence of a conversation about access, but it does not independently establish a coordinated campaign against Shyheim. 

For those interested, feel free to watch the whole interview here:

Still, I understand why revisiting that exchange could bother him. There was nothing wack about Shyheim. Being young did not make his talent a novelty, and having Wu connections did not mean every industry door swung open automatically. Apparently, some doors came with a bouncer and a guest list. He was 15 and maybe younger.

The uncomfortable question is whether the adults remember a funny industry anecdote while the young artist remembers opportunities he never received. Those perspectives can occupy the same room without enjoying each other’s company. By the way, they were not on the phone so I am wondering if he’s referring to some other mysterious clandestine men.

Meanwhile, Wu Maskman is showing love to Shy and also waging his own mini-war on Fat Joe.

And that might be the bigger story here. The kid grew up, found his own microphone, and now has questions for the people who once controlled access to theirs.

item.title: Fat Joe Turns Tiny Desk Into A Bronx Reunion With Remy Ma And Jadakiss
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Fat Joe packed three decades of Bronx rap into a guest-heavy Tiny Desk set featuring Remy Ma, Jadakiss and more.
item.content:encoded:
Fat Joe turned NPR’s Tiny Desk into a Bronx reunion, bringing Remy Ma, Jadakiss, Stove God Cooks, Stevie Mackey and Dre into the room for a career-spanning set released Thursday (November 5).

The Bronx veteran did not walk into NPR headquarters looking for a quiet victory lap. He said he wanted to “touch the third rail,” and the performance kept that promise by moving between records from his early years, Terror Squad staples and material from his latest album, Organized Rhyme.

The show opened with “Million Dollar Intro” before Remy Ma joined Joe for “Cocababy.” From there, he moved through “(Ha Ha) Slow Down” and “I Shot Ya,” then made room for Jadakiss on “New York.” Stove God Cooks, Jadakiss and Remy Ma all returned for “The Aroma,” giving the middle of the set the loose, crowded energy of a New York posse cut instead of a museum piece.

That approach fit the point of the performance. NPR framed the concert around Joe’s loyalty and longevity, and the guest list backed that up. Remy Ma was not brought in for one quick cameo. She stayed central to the final stretch, helping Joe close with “Lean Back” and “All the Way Up,” two records that came from different phases of his career but still land as shared New York anthems.

The live band included music director Zo Harris on keys, Ricky “Strings” Ramos on guitar, Keithan Foster on bass and Antwan “Amadeaus” Thompson on drums. Ted Smooth handled DJ duties, while Dre, one half of Cool & Dre, added background vocals.

The set also gave Joe a compact way to revisit Organized Rhyme, the 12-track album he released in August. Apple Music describes the project as a reunion of Joe’s Bronx-tested delivery and Cool & Dre’s polished production. The album arrived during a year in which Joe also kept building his “Joe and Jada” podcast with Jadakiss, giving their Tiny Desk appearance another layer beyond the old records.

This was Fat Joe’s second Tiny Desk appearance, but his first inside NPR’s office. His 2021 Tiny Desk (Home) performance was filmed at his UP NYC sneaker store during the remote-concert era. Five years later, he came back with a bigger cast and a sharper idea: the catalog matters, but so do the people who helped him build it.

item.title: Yella Beezy Defense Challenges MO3 Witness’s Testimony
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Yella Beezy's lawyers questioned Cedric Bradley's account of MO3's killing and pressed him over his earlier denial.
item.content:encoded:
Yella Beezy’s defense challenged Cedric Bradley’s testimony Kewon White confessed to killing MO3, citing Bradley’s September 2024 denial of knowledge.

The trial continued in Dallas on November 4. Yella Beezy, whose legal name is Markies Conway, pleaded not guilty to capital murder.

Prosecutors accused him of hiring Kewon White to kill his fellow Dallas rapper after a feud. MO3, whose legal name was Melvin Noble, was killed on Interstate 35E on November 11, 2020.

“Your freedom here with the government is a big deal,” a lawyer said, FOX 4 reported.

Bradley faces up to 30 years. His deal dropped a mandatory five-year gun count. Prosecutors said the plea’s June 25 filing preceded their July 10, 2026 meeting.

Bradley’s account had already reached another jury.

During White’s separate trial, he described a visit from White after Bradley returned home from jail. In testimony AllHipHop covered September 1, Bradley said White talked about expecting money and buying another gun once he got paid. The two grew up together in Dallas’ Oak Cliff area.

“He was like, ‘I was the one did that work on that rap nigga on the freeway,'” Bradley testified then.

Bradley also described asking White why he had not received money after the shooting.

“I tell him, I’m like, ‘Damn, you did all that on the freeway or whatever. You ain’t got no money,'” Bradley testified in that earlier proceeding.

White was convicted of capital murder in September and sentenced to life in prison. Yella Beezy’s jury is hearing the allegations against him in a separate trial.

White’s lawyers later sought a new trial over allegations that a juror slept during testimony.

The witness dispute followed a day of testimony about the records prosecutors used to build their payment theory.

FBI Special Agent Taylor Page mapped phones associated with Yella Beezy, White, Devin Brown and Jerry Johnson.

The timeline included Yella Beezy’s $40,000 cash withdrawal in Frisco on November 20, 2020. Johnson’s phone traveled toward Frisco before moving toward White’s phone in South Dallas.

Page said the records showed no direct calls between Yella Beezy and White or Brown. The contacts ran through Johnson.

He also acknowledged that location data could not establish who held a phone or whether people shared a vehicle.

item.title: Cynthia Erivo Joins Snoop Dogg Biopic “Snoop” As Afeni Shakur
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Cynthia Erivo joined Universal's Snoop Dogg biopic as Afeni Shakur, with production underway in Southern California.
item.content:encoded:
Cynthia Erivo has joined Universal’s Snoop Dogg biopic “Snoop” as Afeni Shakur, the activist and businesswoman who raised Tupac Shakur.

The Hollywood Reporter broke the casting news as production continues in Southern California. Jonathan Daviss stars as Snoop while Camron Jones plays Tupac.

Afeni was far more than a famous artist’s mother. She was a Black Panther activist, businesswoman and founder of the Tupac Amaru Shakur Foundation. Tupac honored her struggle and influence in “Dear Mama.”

Casting Erivo puts an award-winning actor in a role tied directly to one of Hip-Hop’s most personal songs.

The ensemble also brings several central figures from Snoop’s rise to life. Myles Bullock will portray Dr. Dre, Lauren London plays Snoop’s mother, Beverly Tate, and Algee Smith takes on Warren G. Tre Hale is Suge Knight, Laya DeLeon Hayes plays Shante Broadus, and Olly Sholotan appears as Kurupt.

Corey Champagne will portray Nate Dogg, Jonica Booth is Lady of Rage, and SwayvoTwain plays Biggie.

Craig Brewer is directing and wrote the latest script draft after Joe Robert Cole handled the original. Brian Grazer, Allan Mandelbaum, Snoop Dogg and Sara Ramaker are producing. The movie will draw from Snoop’s catalog, giving the production direct access to the music that helped build his story.

Universal has set “Snoop” for a wide theatrical release on August 6, 2027, calling it the “definitive biopic” of the Long Beach rap icon.

The project is Death Row Pictures’ first film under its deal with NBCUniversal. The studio made the official announcement in July, months before the latest casting updates.

Erivo enters the film during a busy stretch.

She stars as London trial lawyer Tessa in “Prima Facie,” which opens in U.K. and Irish cinemas on November 13, 2026. She will also appear in “Children of Blood and Bone,” scheduled for January 15, 2027. The Snoop production adds another major role to that run.

For the biopic, Erivo’s job reaches beyond celebrity resemblance. Afeni’s political work, business leadership and role as the Tupac Amaru Shakur Foundation’s founder made her a central figure in Hip-Hop history.

With filming underway, the lineup now spans Snoop’s family, collaborators and several Death Row-era figures central to the story.

item.title: Nicki Minaj May Try To Go Democrat According To New Rumors
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: Nicki Minaj’s political pivot is already in motion and a new rumor says her team wants distance from the MAGA brand.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj might soon need a new explanation for all that MAGA campaigning, if a fresh Media Take Out rumor holds up.

The outlet claims someone in her inner circle says her team has been discussing a political adjustment for months. Supposedly, the plan is to soften her association with the Republican Party while keeping her personal support for Donald Trump intact.

The idea is that she could embrace some moderate Democratic policies. Again…how?

Well, somebody better explain the itinerary. Remember, this is the same woman that came to the rescue on election day against the Blue Wave.

Nicki recently appeared alongside Trump at his Michigan rally, where Republicans Mike Rogers and John James were seeking support. USA Today reported that she helped campaign for those candidates. That makes this alleged distinction between supporting Trump and supporting his party a little harder to sell without follow-up questions.

According to the material MTO published, its unnamed source offered this explanation:

“Nicki’s politics were never squarely Republican,” the source told the outlet.

LOL. People can support individual politicians without subscribing to every position their party takes, right? But when you help promote Republican candidates, the audience is probably going to assume the Republican part matters.

You cannot expect everybody to read the fine print beneath the campaign appearance.

The most interesting part of this rumor is the timing. MTO frames the alleged adjustment as a move coming after Election Day, while also claiming discussions began months ago. Those details invite an obvious question: Is this an existing position finally being clarified, or a proposed image repair job?

We do not have enough evidence to answer that.

And supporting a few Democratic policies would not automatically mean Nicki had become a Democrat. The headline on that particular transformation would need more than an unnamed person’s assurance.

For now, this remains their rumor. I don’t really believe this one, but it’s good content.

If her messaging changes, there will be plenty to examine. Until then, the Barbz might want to keep their MAGA signs.
